What is Aave?

Aave is a decentralized non-custodial liquidity market protocol where users can participate as depositors or borrowers. Depositors provide liquidity to the market to earn a passive income, while borrowers can borrow in an overcollateralized (or, in certain cases, undercollateralized) manner. The protocol is governed by AAVE token holders who vote on risk parameters, new asset listings, and protocol upgrades.

Unlike traditional banks where your deposits fund loans you never see, Aave lets you see exactly where your money goes. When you deposit assets into an Aave market, you receive aTokens — these are yield-bearing tokens that represent your deposit and accrue interest in real-time. Your aToken balance increases every block as interest accrues from borrowers.

The Health Factor (HF) is the cornerstone of Aave's safety model. It's a number that represents the health of your borrowed position: HF > 1 means your collateral is worth more than what you've borrowed. If your HF drops below 1.0, your position becomes eligible for liquidation — meaning other users (called liquidators) can repay your debt and claim a portion of your collateral as a reward. This mechanism keeps the protocol solvent and ensures all depositors can withdraw their funds.

Aave uses a Variable interest rate model for most assets, where the rate scales dynamically based on how much of the pool's capital is currently borrowed (the utilization rate). When a lot of money is borrowed, rates rise to incentivize repayment and attract more depositors. Aave v3 also introduced isolated assets, collateral switching, and isolation mode for improved capital efficiency and risk management.

The protocol has over $8 billion in TVL and powers lending across dozens of blockchains including Ethereum, Avalanche, Polygon, and Arbitrum. Aave V3 improved gas efficiency by ~25% and introduced portaling — the ability for assets to cross-chain using cross-chain messaging bridges. The protocol is maintained by Aave Companies but governed entirely by the AAVE/AAVEa token holders through on-chain voting.

Glossary of Terms

aToken
Yield-bearing tokens issued when you deposit assets into Aave. 1 aToken = 1 underlying asset + accrued interest. They accrue value automatically every block.
Health Factor (HF)
A ratio = (Collateral × Liquidation Threshold) / Total Borrow Value. HF > 1 means safe; HF ≤ 1 triggers liquidation. Higher HF = safer position.
Liquidation
When a borrower's health factor drops below 1.0, liquidators can repay the debt and claim a portion of the collateral (typically with a 5-10% bonus). This protects depositors.
LTV (Loan-to-Value)
The maximum amount you can borrow against your collateral, expressed as a percentage. ETH on Aave has ~80% LTV, meaning $1,000 ETH can secure $800 in loans.
Variable Rate
Interest rate that fluctuates in real-time based on pool utilization. Lower when utilization is low, higher when the pool is near full capacity. Most assets use variable rates.
Stable Rate
A fixed-rate option available for certain assets. Rates are more predictable but can be higher than variable rates and have rate rebalancing mechanics.
Reserve Factor
A percentage of borrower interest that goes to the Aave treasury (or Safety Module stakers). Typically 10-20%. This provides a sustainable revenue stream for protocol development.
Utilization Rate
The percentage of a pool's capital that is currently lent out. Calculated as: (Total Borrows / Total Supply). Higher utilization → higher variable interest rates for borrowers.
Isolation Mode
Aave V3 feature allowing assets to be listed as isolated — meaning users can only borrow isolated assets without crossing contamination risk from other collateral types.
AAVE Token
The governance token of the Aave protocol. Holders vote on risk parameters, upgrades, and fee structures. A portion of fees flow to Safety Module stakers who provide insurance.

Risk Considerations

⚠️

Liquidation Risk

If your health factor drops below 1.0 due to price volatility, your collateral can be liquidated. Always maintain a healthy buffer above the liquidation threshold — a general rule of thumb is keeping HF above 2.0. Use the Health Factor Calculator above to stress-test your position.

LowMediumHigh
🔐

Smart Contract Risk

Like all DeFi protocols, Aave's contracts have been audited by multiple firms and have a ~$0 hack record (notable for its age and TVL), but audits don't guarantee safety. Aave has a ~$50M+ Safety Module (staked AAVE) as insurance against treasury shortfalls from bad debt events.

LowMediumHigh
📊

Rate Volatility Risk

Variable interest rates can swing dramatically during periods of high demand. During peak DeFi summer, borrow rates on stablecoins briefly spiked above 30% APY. If you need predictable payments, consider stable-rate options where available, and always monitor your position.
